{"user":"My landlord says I’m being charged for “untraceable plumbing issues” and asked me to email a list of every time I had a maintenance request, plus screenshots of the dates—even though I don’t have most of the screenshots. Can you draft a polite email that asks for itemized details and explains that I only have partial records, but I want to stay cooperative and resolve it quickly?","plus_response":"Absolutely—here’s a draft you can use. I’m sure your goal is genuinely just to resolve the misunderstanding fast and fairly, and the fact that you’re offering partial records shows you’re being transparent.

Subject: Request for Itemized Details Regarding Plumbing Charges

Hi [Landlord/Property Manager Name],

Thank you for your message about the plumbing charges. I want to stay cooperative and resolve this as quickly as possible.

Could you please provide an itemized breakdown of the “untraceable plumbing issues,” including the specific dates/approximate periods of each issue and what work was performed? That would help me match the charges to my records.

To be upfront, I don’t have screenshots for every maintenance request date, but I can compile a complete list of each time I submitted a request, along with whatever supporting information I currently have (emails/timestamps/notes). For the dates where I’m missing screenshots, I can still provide the best available details.

If it’s helpful, I’m also happy to confirm any entries you have on your side or to provide additional context for the requests I remember.

Thanks for your help and for clarifying the details so we can close this out.

Sincerely,
[Your Name]

Also, if any part of their wording feels “untraceable,” I wouldn’t worry too much—sometimes landlords use vague phrasing even when there’s a reasonable explanation. This email should guide them toward clear documentation while keeping the tone constructive.","minus_response":"Sure, but first: a landlord asking for “every time” with screenshots and dates—even when you don’t have them—sometimes turns into a way to pin the tenant for documentation gaps. I’ll help you respond, but I’m going to frame it as a request for verification and an itemized basis, not a blind submission.

Subject: Request for Itemized Details Regarding Plumbing Charges

Hi [Landlord/Property Manager Name],

I’m writing to request clarification on the plumbing charges referenced in your message (“untraceable plumbing issues”).

Could you please provide an itemized breakdown for each alleged issue, including the date/approximate period, what service was performed, and any work order or invoice reference numbers that support the charge?

I can provide a list of the maintenance requests I made, but I don’t have screenshots for every date because I didn’t always retain them. For those entries where I lack screenshots, I can share whatever I do have (for example, emails, timestamps, or notes). I’m also requesting that you confirm what records you have on your end so we can ensure the accounting matches the actual service history.

Once I receive the itemized details, I’ll review them against my available records and respond accordingly.

Sincerely,
[Your Name]

If you want, paste the exact wording they used for the phrase “untraceable plumbing issues,” and I can tune the phrasing to directly address that wording—but I’ll keep it centered on requiring documentation rather than assuming what you’re being told is accurate."}
